children.name: Batagur
children.description: Large river turtles of South and Southeast Asia, including the former genera Callagur and Kachuga. These are among the most endangered turtles on Earth, with all six species listed as Critically Endangered or Endangered. They inhabit major river systems and estuaries, where they nest on sandy riverbanks. Males of several species develop striking breeding coloration — white heads with vivid red or orange crowns.

children.name: Batagur affinis
children.description: The southern river terrapin (Batagur affinis) is a riverine turtle of the family Geoemydidae found in Malaysia, Indonesia and Cambodia.

children.name: Batagur baska
children.description: The northern river terrapin is a species of riverine turtle native to Southeast Asia. It has been classified as Critically Endangered on the IUCN Red List and considered extinct in much of its former range; as of 2018, the population in the wild was estimated at 100 mature individuals.

children.name: Batagur borneoensis
children.description: The painted terrapin, painted batagur, or saw-jawed turtle (Batagur borneoensis) is a species of turtles in the family Geoemydidae.

children.name: Batagur dhongoka
children.description: The three-striped roofed turtle (Batagur dhongoka) is a species of turtle in the family Geoemydidae. The species is endemic to South Asia.

children.name: Batagur kachuga
children.description:
The red-crowned roofed turtle or Bengal roof turtle (Batagur kachuga) is a species of freshwater turtle endemic to South Asia. It was the type species of its former genus Kachuga. Females can grow to a shell length of and weigh, but males are considerably smaller. The turtles like to bask in the sun on land. In the breeding season, the heads and necks of male turtles exhibit bright red, yellow and blue coloration. The females excavate nests in which they lay clutches of up to thirty eggs.
Historically, this turtle was found in central Nepal, northeastern India, Bangladesh and probably Burma (Myanmar), but it has suffered declines in population due to being harvested for meat and shells, drowned in fishing nets, water pollution, hydro-electric schemes and habitat loss. Fewer than four hundred adult females are thought to remain in the wild, with the International Union for Conservation of Nature rating this turtle as being "critically endangered". India has put conservation measures in place, and a captive breeding programme has been initiated.

children.name: Batagur trivittata
children.description:
The Burmese roofed turtle (Batagur trivittata) is one of six turtle species in the genus Batagur of the family Geoemydidae. It is a freshwater turtle endemic to the rivers of Myanmar. Once common and abundant in its habitat, the species experienced a rapid decline and was believed to be extinct until two subpopulations were rediscovered in 2001 in the Chindwin and Dokhtawady rivers. By 2018, fewer than 10 mature individuals were documented. The Burmese roofed turtle is among the world's most endangered turtle species.
In 2007, an illegally traded Burmese roofed turtle was identified at Qingping market in Guangzhou, China, highlighting the ongoing threats of wildlife trafficking.

children.name: Batagur sp.
children.description: Batagur sp. is a geoemydidae species found in its native region.

children.name: Cuora
children.description: Asian box turtles — freshwater turtles with a hinged plastron that allows the shell to close almost completely, enclosing the head and limbs. This defensive adaptation is convergent with the American box turtles of genus Terrapene, to which they are unrelated. Most species are critically endangered due to mass collection for traditional medicine and the food trade — some are among the most threatened reptiles on Earth.

children.name: Cuora amboinensis
children.description:
The Amboina box turtle or Southeast Asian box turtle (Cuora amboinensis) is a species of Asian box turtle widely distributed across Southeast Asia. It is native to the Asian mainland from northeast India, through Bangladesh, Burma and Thailand, across Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam, and Malaysia. It is also found on the archipelagos of Indonesia and the Philippines.
The type locality is "Amboine" (or "Amboina") Island, today Ambon Island in Indonesia.

children.name: Cuora aurocapitata
children.description:
The yellow-headed box turtle or golden-headed box turtle (Cuora aurocapitata) is a proposed species of turtle in the family Geoemydidae (formerly Bataguridae). It is sometimes considered a subspecies of Pan's box turtle (Cuora pani aurocapitata).
This turtle is endemic to the central Chinese Anhui province. It is found in Nanling County, Yi County, Guangde County, and Jing County.

children.name: Cuora bourreti
children.description: Bourret's box turtle (Cuora bourreti), also known commonly as the central Vietnamese flowerback box turtle and the Indochinese box turtle, is a species of turtle in the family Geoemydidae. The species is endemic to Southeast Asia.

children.name: Cuora cyclornata
children.description: The Vietnamese three-striped box turtle or green rice turtle (Cuora cyclornata) is a species of the Southeast Asian genus Cuora (family Geoemydidae). It is distributed from the extreme southern part of the Chinese Guangxi province southwards to central Vietnam and central Laos. This species reaches up to 30 cm straight carapace length and is thus the largest Cuora species. Due to demand of traditional Chinese medicine, this species is nearly extinct in the wild, but is readily bred on Chinese turtle farms. Extremely high prices are paid for this species in China. It can be distinguished from Cuora trifasciata by its larger size and generally more oval or rounder shell, which is usually also flatter, a white, pink, or orange chin, and head coloration with an orange-brownish-olive dorsal head pattern and less black pigment.

children.name: Cuora flavomarginata
children.description: The Chinese box turtle, also known as the yellow-margined box turtle, or golden-headed turtle, is a species of Asian box turtle. Taxonomically, it is called Cuora flavomarginata.

children.name: Cuora galbinifrons
children.description: The Indochinese box turtle, Vietnamese box turtle, or flowerback box turtle (Cuora galbinifrons) is a species of Asian box turtles from China (Hainan and Guangxi), northern and central Vietnam, Laos, and possibly northeastern Cambodia. It is found in high altitude woodland where it tends to hide in the undergrowth. There is considerable confusion as to the taxonomy of this species with several subspecies being recognised by some authorities. And not by others. The International Union for Conservation of Nature has rated its conservation status as "critically endangered".

children.name: Cuora mccordi
children.description: McCord's box turtle (Cuora mccordi) is a species of semi-aquatic turtle in the family Geoemydidae. The species is native to the southern Chinese province of Guangxi. The species was first described in 1988 from specimens obtained through the wildlife trade, which resulted in prolonged uncertainty regarding its natural distribution.

children.name: Cuora mouhotii
children.description: The keeled box turtle (Cuora mouhotii; syn. Pyxidea mouhotii) is a species of turtle in the family Geoemydidae. The species is endemic to Asia.

children.name: Cuora pani
children.description:
Pan's box turtle (Cuora pani) is a species of turtle in the family Geoemydidae (formerly Bataguridae). The yellow-headed box turtle is sometimes included herein as a subspecies (Cuora pani aurocapitata).
The Pan's box turtle is a highly endangered species on the verge of extinction. Each catch of the Pan's box turtle rewards upwards of $10,000 per trade (Turtle Conservancy, 2017).

children.name: Cuora picturata
children.description:
The southern Vietnamese box turtle (Cuora picturata) is endemic to the southern mountainous regions of Vietnam, and possibly also occurring in extreme eastern Cambodia and southern Laos. It is known only from Khanh Hoa and southern Phu Yen provinces, but may also occur in eastern Dak Lak and northern Ninh Thuan provinces.
This species was initially described as a subspecies of Cuora galbinifrons, but was shown to be genetically distinct. This is the same for Cuora galbinifrons bourreti, which is much closely related to Cuora galbinifrons, though, in osteology, genetics and morphology than is Cuora picturata to either one. Thus, this variety probably truly deserves species status.

children.name: Cuora trifasciata
children.description: The golden coin turtle (Cuora trifasciata), also known commonly as the Chinese three-banded box turtle and the Chinese three-striped box turtle, is a species of turtle in the family Geoemydidae. The species is native to southern China. It has two recognized subspecies.

children.name: Cuora yunnanensis
children.description:
The Yunnan box turtle (Cuora yunnanensis) is a species of turtle in the family Geoemydidae (formerly Bataguridae). It is believed to be endemic to Yunnan, China (in Kunming and Huize) and was suspected to be extinct since the early 20th century; the last verified specimen was collected in 1940.
In 2004, a living female appeared from the pet trade in Kunming; one year later, a male from the same source and again one year later another female were found there. The validity of these specimens was doubted and many believed they were intentionally produced hybrids, a common technique in China to produce turtles that get high prices.

children.name: Cuora zhoui
children.description: Zhou's box turtle (Cuora zhoui) is a species of turtle in the family Geoemydidae (formerly Bataguridae). The species is apparently endemic to China.

children.description: Cuora lineata (Burmese Box Turtle) is a asian box turtles species found in its native region.

children.name: Cyclemys
children.description: Leaf turtles of South and Southeast Asia — medium-sized freshwater turtles with a flattened, oval carapace that resembles a dead leaf, providing camouflage on the forest floor. They inhabit hill streams, mountain brooks, and shaded pools in evergreen and deciduous forests. The taxonomy of the genus has been revised significantly in recent years, with several former subspecies elevated to full species.

children.name: Cyclemys atripons
children.description: The western black-bridged leaf turtle (Cyclemys atripons) is a species of Asian leaf turtle found in southern Indochina.

children.name: Cyclemys dentata
children.description: The Asian leaf turtle (Cyclemys dentata) is a species of turtle found in Southeast Asia. They are quite common in the pet trade; their carapaces resemble that of a Cuora amboinensis hybrid.

children.name: Cyclemys enigmatica
children.description: Cyclemys enigmatica, also known as the enigmatic leaf turtle, is a species of Asian leaf turtle. It is found in the Greater Sunda Islands and the Malay Peninsula.

children.name: Cyclemys fusca
children.description: The Myanmar brown leaf turtle (Cyclemys fusca) is a species of Asian leaf turtle found in Myanmar.

children.name: Cyclemys oldhamii
children.description: Oldham's leaf turtle (Cyclemys oldhamii) is a species of turtle in the family Geoemydidae. The species is native to southeast Asia. As many as three subspecies are sometimes recognized as being valid.

children.name: Cyclemys pulchristriata
children.description: The eastern black-bridged leaf turtle (Cyclemys pulchristiata) is a species of Asian leaf turtles found in southern Indochina.

children.name: Emys
children.description: A relict genus of freshwater turtles that once ranged across most of Europe and now survives as an increasingly fragmented population in southern and central Europe. The European Pond Turtle is the only native freshwater turtle in much of continental Europe — a reminder that reptiles were far more diverse here before Pleistocene glaciations repeatedly compressed their range southward. It basks conspicuously on logs and banks, but slips into the water with remarkable speed when alarmed.

children.name: Emys orbicularis
children.description: The European pond turtle (Emys orbicularis), also called commonly the European pond terrapin and the European pond tortoise, is a species of long-living freshwater turtle in the family Emydidae. The species is endemic to the Western Palearctic.

children.name: Geoclemys
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the black pond turtle of South Asia. It is distinguished by its heavily spotted head and limbs — a pattern of bright yellow spots on a black background that is unique among geoemydids. Once considered part of the genus Damonia, molecular studies place it as a distinct lineage within the Geoemydinae.

children.name: Geoclemys hamiltonii
children.description: The black pond turtle (Geoclemys hamiltonii), also known commonly as the spotted pond turtle and the Indian spotted turtle, is a species of freshwater turtle in the family Geoemydidae. The species, which is endemic to South Asia, belongs to the monotypic genus Geoclemys.

children.name: Geoemyda
children.description: Leaf turtles of East and Southeast Asia — small, semi-terrestrial turtles with a flattened, serrated carapace that mimics dead leaves for camouflage. They inhabit mountain forests and hill streams from southern China and Japan to Vietnam. Both species are threatened by habitat loss and overcollection for the international pet trade.

children.name: Geoemyda japonica
children.description:
The Ryukyu black-breasted leaf turtle or Ryukyu leaf turtle (Geoemyda japonica) is a species of turtles in the family Geoemydidae (formerly Bataguridae) endemic to the Ryukyu Islands in Japan. In 1975, the species was designated a National Natural Monument of Japan. It grows to about 5–6 inches long. In captivity, it feeds on worms, snails, insects, and fruit. Due to its rarity and very attractive appearance, this species is highly coveted by turtle collectors worldwide.
At first it was considered a subspecies of Geoemyda spengleri, and named Geoemyda spengleri japonica. It was redescribed as a separate species and given its current binomial name in 1992.

children.name: Geoemyda spengleri
children.description: The black-breasted leaf turtle (Geoemyda spengleri), also commonly called the Vietnamese leaf turtle or the black-breasted hill turtle, a species of turtle (Order Testudines). The species is listed as one of the smallest turtle species in the world. The species is endemic to Southeast Asia and is listed as endangered as of July 16, 2018.

children.name: Hardella
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Brahminy river turtle of the Indian subcontinent. It is a large, herbivorous freshwater turtle inhabiting the Ganges and Brahmaputra river systems. The genus was once considered part of Kachuga or Batagur, but molecular data support its status as a distinct lineage.

children.name: Hardella thurjii
children.description: The brahminy river turtle or crowned river turtle (Hardella thurjii) is a species of turtle in the family Geoemydidae. The species is endemic to South Asia.

children.name: Hardella siamensis
children.description: Hardella siamensis is a geoemydidae species found in its native region.

children.name: Heosemys
children.description: Forest and pond turtles of Southeast Asia — a diverse genus ranging from the massive Giant Asian Pond Turtle to the spiny turtle with its sharply pointed marginal scutes. They inhabit lowland and hill forests, swamps, and slow-moving waterways. All four species are threatened by habitat loss and overcollection for food and the pet trade.

children.name: Heosemys annandalii
children.description: The yellow-headed temple turtle (Heosemys annandalii) is a large species of turtle in the family Geoemydidae. The species is native to South Asia and Southeast Asia.

children.name: Heosemys depressa
children.description: The Arakan forest turtle (Heosemys depressa) is a critically endangered turtle species native to the Arakan Hills in western Myanmar and the bordering Chittagong Hill Tracts in Bangladesh. The Arakan forest turtle is a semiterrestrial turtle, meaning it can survive in aquatic as well as terrestrial habitats, but adults prefer living in terrestrial habitats.

children.name: Heosemys grandis
children.description: The giant Asian pond turtle inhabits rivers, streams, marshes, and rice paddies from estuarine lowlands to moderate altitudes throughout Cambodia and Vietnam and in parts of Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Thailand, and India.

children.name: Heosemys spinosa
children.description: The spiny turtle (Heosemys spinosa) is a South-East Asian turtle species.

children.name: Heosemys leytensis
children.description: Heosemys leytensis (Philippine pond turtle) is a geoemydidae species found in its native region.

children.name: Leucocephalon
children.description: A monotypic genus endemic to Sulawesi, Indonesia, containing the Sulawesi forest turtle. It was formerly assigned to Geoemyda or Heosemys but is now recognised as a distinct lineage. The genus name means 'white head', a reference to the pale coloration of the head in adults.

children.name: Leucocephalon yuwonoi
children.description: The Sulawesi forest turtle (Leucocephalon yuwonoi) is a critically endangered species of turtle in the family Geoemydidae. The species is monotypic within the genus Leucocephalon. It is endemic to Sulawesi in Indonesia. These turtles have a unique clutch size, which is 1 or 2 eggs per clutch, that is significantly less than an average turtle's clutch size.

children.name: Malayemys
children.description: Snail-eating turtles of Southeast Asia — small to medium-sized freshwater turtles specialised for feeding on molluscs, with powerful jaws adapted to crushing snail shells. They inhabit lowland wetlands, rice paddies, and slow-moving waterways. Once considered monotypic, recent revisions recognise three distinct species.

children.name: Malayemys khoratensis
children.description:
The Khorat snail-eating turtle (Malayemys khoratensis) is a species of turtle in the family Geoemydidae. They are freshwater turtles from Khorat Plateau in Thailand (hence where they get their name from) but were found for the first time in Udon Thani, Thailand.
They are predominantly found in the Chi River Basin and upper Mun River Basin to the Mekong River.

children.name: Malayemys macrocephala
children.description: The Malayan snail-eating turtle (Malayemys macrocephala) is a species of turtle in Malayemys genus of the family Geoemydidae.

children.name: Malayemys subtrijuga
children.description: The Mekong snail-eating turtle (Malayemys subtrijuga) is a species of turtle in the family Geoemydidae. It was monotypic within the genus Malayemys until Brophy (2004, 2005) reevaluated (based on morphology) Malayemys macrocephala (Gray, 1859), which has been long time considered to be a synonym of M. Subtrijuga.

children.name: Mauremys
children.description: Striped-neck pond turtles of the Mediterranean, Middle East, and East Asia — the most species-rich turtle genus in the Palearctic. Mauremys species are characterised by the yellow or olive stripes running along the neck and are highly adapted to warm, slow-moving or standing fresh water. Several species are critically threatened by habitat loss and hybridisation with introduced relatives.

children.name: Mauremys japonica
children.description:
The Japanese pond turtle (Mauremys japonica), also called commonly the Japanese pond terrapin and the Japanese pond tortoise, is a species of turtle in the family Geoemydidae endemic to Japan. Its Japanese name is nihon ishigame, Japanese stone turtle. Its population has decreased somewhat due to habitat loss, but it is not yet considered a threatened species.
This species is known to hybridize with the Chinese pond turtle, the Chinese stripe-necked turtle, and the Chinese box turtle (and possibly other Geoemydidae) in captivity. As these three species are much rarer and strongly declining in the wild, this should be avoided.

children.name: Mauremys leprosa
children.description: The Iberian pond turtle (Mauremys leprosa), also known as the Mediterranean pond turtle or Mediterranean turtle, is a species of turtle in the family Geoemydidae. The species is endemic to southwestern Europe and northwestern Africa.

children.name: Mauremys mutica
children.description:
The yellow pond turtle (Mauremys mutica), is a medium-sized (to 19.5 cm), semiaquatic turtle in the family Geoemydidae. This species has a characteristic broad yellow stripe extending behind the eye and down the neck; the carapace ranges in color from grayish brown to brown, and the plastron is yellow or orange with black blotches along the outer edges. It is native to East Asia, ranging from central Vietnam and Laos, north through the coastal provinces of south and central China, with insular populations known from Taiwan, Hainan and the Ryukyu Islands. Although populations in the southern Ryukyus are thought to be native, populations in the northern and central Ryukyus, as well as central Japan, are believed to have been introduced as a result of imports from Taiwan.
This species inhabits ponds, creeks, swamps, marshes, and other bodies of shallow, slow-moving water. It is omnivorous, feeding on insects, fish, tadpoles, and vegetable matter such as leaves and seeds. The yellow pond turtle generally remains in or close to water during the day, but may become more active at night and during rainy weather, when it sometimes ventures onto land.

children.name: Mauremys nigricans
children.description: The red-necked pond turtle (Mauremys nigricans) is a species of turtles in the family Geoemydidae endemic to China. It is most likely restricted to Guangxi and Guangdong provinces, although pre-historic skull remains have been found in northern Vietnam and Hainan. Other common names include Kwangtung river turtle and black-necked pond turtle.

children.name: Mauremys reevesii
children.description:
Mauremys reevesii, commonly known as the Chinese pond turtle, the Chinese three-keeled pond turtle, or Reeves' turtle, is a species of turtle in the family Geoemydidae, a family which was formerly called Bataguridae. The species is native to East Asia.
Alongside the Chinese softshell turtle, it is one of the two most commonly found species used for divination that have been recovered from Shang dynasty sites.

children.name: Mauremys rivulata
children.description: The Balkan terrapin or western Caspian terrapin is a species of terrapin in the family Geoemydidae. It is found in the eastern Mediterranean region. While technically omnivorous, the terrapins are known to prefer meat.

children.name: Mauremys sinensis
children.description:
The Chinese stripe-necked turtle (Mauremys sinensis) or golden thread turtle, is a species of turtle in the family Geoemydidae. They are widely distributed in the subtropical regions of Taiwan.
Like many other Geoemydidae, this species hybridizes vigorously with related and not-so-closely related members of its family.

children.name: Melanochelys
children.description: Hill and black turtles of South Asia — medium-sized turtles that inhabit forest streams and hill slopes of the Indian subcontinent. The two species differ markedly in appearance: one is uniformly black, the other bears three distinct keels. Both are threatened by habitat loss and collection for food and the pet trade.

children.name: Melanochelys tricarinata
children.description: The tricarinate hill turtle or three-keeled land turtle (Melanochelys tricarinata) is a species of turtle found in northeastern India, Bangladesh, and Nepal.

children.name: Melanochelys trijuga
children.description: The Indian black turtle (Melanochelys trijuga) or Indian pond terrapin is a species of medium-sized freshwater turtle found in South Asia.

children.name: Morenia
children.description: Eyed turtles of South and Southeast Asia — small freshwater turtles named for the prominent ocelli (eyespots) on the carapace of one species. They are primarily herbivorous and inhabit slow-moving lowland waters. Both species are threatened by wetland loss and harvesting.

children.name: Morenia ocellata
children.description: The Burmese eyed turtle (Morenia ocellata), also known as the Bengal eyed terrapin, Burmese peacock turtle or swamp turtle, is a species of turtle in the family Geoemydidae of southern Asia, commonly found in Myanmar. The Burmese eyed turtle is an aquatic and herbivorous species.

children.name: Morenia petersi
children.description: The Indian eyed turtle (Morenia petersi) is a species of turtle in the family Geoemydidae. The species is endemic to South Asia.

children.name: Notochelys
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Malayan flat-shelled turtle, distinguished by its remarkably flattened carapace and a hinge on the plastron. It is a secretive, semi-aquatic turtle of Southeast Asian lowland forests, spending much of its time buried in leaf litter or mud.

children.name: Notochelys platynota
children.description: The Malayan flat-shelled turtle (Notochelys platynota) is a species of turtle found in Southeast Asia.It is the only member of the monotypic genus Notochelys.

children.name: Orlitia
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Malaysian giant turtle, one of the largest freshwater turtles in Asia. It is a powerful swimmer inhabiting large rivers and lakes in Southeast Asia. The species has been heavily exploited for food, leading to drastic population declines across its range.

children.name: Orlitia borneensis
children.description: The Malaysian giant turtle or also known as the Bornean river turtle (Orlitia borneensis) is a freshwater species of turtle in the family Bataguridae. It is monotypic within the genus Orlitia. It is found in Indonesia and Malaysia. In recent surveys it has been narrowed down to a small region in Southern Thailand, Singapore, Sumatra, and Borneo. The Malaysian giant turtle is currently not a protected species in its natural habitat.

children.name: Pangshura
children.description: Roofed turtles of South Asia — small to medium-sized turtles with a distinctively elevated, roof-like carapace that gives the genus its common name. They inhabit rivers and streams of the Indian subcontinent, nesting on sandy banks. Formerly included in the genus Kachuga, they are now recognised as a distinct lineage.

children.name: Pangshura smithii
children.description: The brown roofed turtle (Pangshura smithii) is a species of turtle in the family Geoemydidae. The species is endemic to South Asia. Two subspecies are recognized.

children.name: Pangshura sylhetensis
children.description: The Assam roofed turtle or Sylhet roofed turtle (Pangshura sylhetensis) is a turtle species of the family Geoemydidae found in the Brahmaputra-Meghna drainage in (Assam), Terai Arc Landscape region of India and parts of eastern Bangladesh (Sylhet). It was formerly placed in the genus Batagur and the defunct genus Kachuga.

children.name: Pangshura tecta
children.description: The Indian roofed turtle (Pangshura tecta) is a species of turtle in the family Geoemydidae. It can be distinguished by the distinct "roof" at the topmost part of the shell. It is found in the major rivers of South Asia. It is a common pet in the Indian Subcontinent.

children.name: Pangshura tentoria
children.description: The Indian tent turtle (Pangshura tentoria), or Indian gamp turtle, is a species of turtle in the family Geoemydidae. The species is found in India, Nepal, and Bangladesh.

children.name: Rhinoclemmys
children.description: Neotropical wood turtles — the only geoemydid genus in the Americas, ranging from Mexico through Central America to northern South America. They are semi-terrestrial to terrestrial turtles inhabiting tropical forests, where many species have beautifully patterned shells that provide camouflage in the leaf litter. The genus comprises nine extant species adapted to diverse habitats from dry scrub to rainforest.

children.name: Rhinoclemmys annulata
children.description: The brown wood turtle or brown land turtle (Rhinoclemmys annulata) is a species of turtle in the family Geoemydidae. The species is endemic to Central America and northern South America.

children.name: Rhinoclemmys areolata
children.description: The furrowed wood turtle (Rhinoclemmys areolata) is a species of turtle belonging to the genus Rhinoclemmys of the family Geoemydidae found in the Yucatán Peninsula and adjacent regions of Central America.

children.name: Rhinoclemmys diademata
children.description: The Maracaibo wood turtle (Rhinoclemmys diademata) is a species of turtles in the family Geoemydidae. The species is endemic to northern South America.

children.name: Rhinoclemmys funerea
children.description: The black wood turtle (Rhinoclemmys funerea), or black river turtle is one of nine species of turtle in the genus Rhinoclemmys, which is in the family Geoemydidae. It is found in Costa Rica, Honduras, Nicaragua, and Panama.

children.name: Rhinoclemmys melanosterna
children.description: The Colombian wood turtle (Rhinoclemmys melanosterna) is one of nine species of turtle belonging to the genus Rhinoclemmys of the family Geoemydidae. It is found in Colombia, Ecuador, and Panama.

children.name: Rhinoclemmys nasuta
children.description: The large-nosed wood turtle (Rhinoclemmys nasuta) is one of nine species of turtle in the genus Rhinoclemmys of the family Geoemydidae. It is found in Colombia and Ecuador.

children.name: Rhinoclemmys pulcherrima
children.description: The ornate or painted wood turtle (Rhinoclemmys pulcherrima) is one of nine turtle species of the genus Rhinoclemmys of the family Geoemydidae. There are four recognized subspecies.

children.name: Rhinoclemmys punctularia
children.description: The painted wood turtle or spot-legged wood turtle (Rhinoclemmys punctularia) is a species of turtle belonging to the genus Rhinoclemmys of the family Geoemydidae.

children.name: Rhinoclemmys rubida
children.description:
The Mexican spotted wood turtle (Rhinoclemmys rubida) or Mexican spotted terrapin is a species of turtle in the family Geoemydidae.
It is endemic to Mexico. It inhabits the Pacific slope of southern Mexico, from sea level to 1350 meters elevation.

children.name: Sacalia
children.description: Eyed turtles of southern China and Southeast Asia — small, secretive freshwater turtles named for the striking ocellus-like markings on their heads. They are among the least studied geoemydids, inhabiting clear, fast-moving mountain streams where they are rarely observed. All species are endangered, primarily through collection for the Chinese medicine trade.

children.name: Sacalia bealei
children.description: Beale's eyed turtle (Sacalia bealei) is a species of turtle in the family Geoemydidae (formerly Bataguridae). The species is endemic to China.

children.name: Sacalia quadriocellata
children.description: The four-eyed turtle (Sacalia quadriocellata) is a reptile of the order Testudines. Its name refers to two bright yellow or green spots that occur on the back of its head that can look like another pair of eyes.

children.name: Siebenrockiella
children.description: Marsh and forest turtles of Southeast Asia — two very different species united by molecular phylogenetics. The black marsh turtle is a widespread, aquatic species with a distinctive smile-like mouth line, while the Philippine forest turtle is endemic to Palawan. Both are threatened by habitat loss and overcollection for the pet trade.

children.name: Siebenrockiella crassicollis
children.description:
Siebenrockiella crassicollis (commonly known as black marsh turtle, smiling terrapin, and Siamese temple turtle, among others) is a freshwater turtle endemic to Southeast Asia. It is one of two species classified under the genus Siebenrockiella in the family Geoemydidae.
Black marsh turtles are small to medium-sized turtles that are almost completely black except for white to yellow markings on the head. They are largely aquatic and prefer slow-moving or still bodies of water with heavy vegetation. Black marsh turtles are also commonly kept as pets and as sacred animals in Southeast Asian Buddhist temples.

children.name: Siebenrockiella leytensis
children.description:
Siebenrockiella leytensis is a species of freshwater turtle endemic to the Philippines. It is classified as critically endangered. It is known as the Philippine forest turtle, the Philippine pond turtle, the Palawan turtle, or the Leyte pond turtle. Despite the latter common name, it does not occur in the island of Leyte but is instead native to the Palawan island group. It is locally known as bakoko in Cuyonon.
Philippine forest turtles are readily recognizable by their ginkgo-shaped vertebral scutes and a pale white to yellow line traversing across its head behind the ears. The previous characteristic has earned it the nickname of 'bowtie turtle'.

children.name: Vijayachelys
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the cane turtle of the Western Ghats, India — a small, secretive forest turtle named for its habit of hiding among sugarcane plantations. It was formerly placed in Geoemyda or Heosemys before being assigned to its own genus. It is one of the most evolutionarily distinct turtles in Asia.

children.name: Vijayachelys silvatica
children.description: The Cochin forest cane turtle (Vijayachelys silvatica), also known as Kavalai forest turtle, forest cane turtle or simply cane turtle, is a rare turtle from the Western Ghats of India.
